what_happened: The job "Add code-health check, status table, and design-review cadence" (20261026-042558-5p65) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 1 of 3 the critic said the plan needed revising and judged that the reading misread the request. It confirmed the plan's code references exist (note_finished, land_pr, REQUEST_CHANNEL, StatusView, CheckRun.duration) and that each demonstration would fail without the behavior. The one problem was that the reading assumed a design-review role from job 20261017-205558-dn2e already exists. The critic found no such role, prompt or text in the snapshot, so the queued periodic review request has to carry its own content. There were three other minor findings and a nit: the land_pr hook has no test, the queued requests have no acceptance bullets, and the first review may fire at once on existing history. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria, no blocker or major findings, and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Nothing checks a reading's references to earlier jobs against the current repo. A job id named in the request or notes is taken to mean its work has landed. The earlier job may be queued, unmerged or never produced. The critic is the first stage to search the snapshot, so the gap appears only in planning. Minor findings and a nit also made the critic return "needs revising", which stopped the job. The request also gave no required content for the review it asked to be queued.
prevention: Add a check at reading acceptance. For every earlier job id, role, prompt or file the reading calls existing, it confirms the artifact is in the snapshot (landed in main, with a path found). If not, the reading must either list it as a deliverable of this job or make the dependency explicit and unmet. A request that queues a recurring review must carry the review's full content and acceptance bullets in the same job.
proposed_request: Add a code-health check, a status table and a design-review cadence. (1) A standing check measures code size and churn against thresholds, derived from records so it does not double count. It runs when a job finishes and when a pull request lands. (2) The status view shows a code-health table with each measure, its threshold and whether it is over. (3) After a set number of landings since the last design review request, Athena queues a design-review request on the steward channel. That request must carry its own full text: what to review (module size, churn, duplicated logic, boundaries), what the output is (a written findings page and follow-up requests, each with acceptance bullets), and how the review is judged done. Do not assume a design-review role from job 20261017-205558-dn2e exists. It is not in the repo, so define the review content in this job. If no earlier review request exists, set the cadence baseline to the job's landing so the first review does not fire at once on existing history. Add a test showing the land_pr hook runs the check. Add no athena.toml field. Acceptance: tests show the check flags a size breach and stays quiet under the threshold; the status table lists the measures; the queued review request has the full text and acceptance bullets; the first review does not fire at once; the land_pr hook test fails without the hook.
